chunks: 1551 - Murazim narrated from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“If one of you intends something, then let him perform two rak'ahs, then let him praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and say: O Allah, if this matter is good for me in my religion and my worldly life, then make it easy for me and decree it for me; and if it is otherwise than that, then turn it away from me.”
Murazim said: So I asked, “What is to be recited in them?” He said: “Recite in them whatever you wish. If you wish, then recite in them,”
“‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ and ‘Qul ya ayyuhal kafirun’”
and “‘Qul huwa Allahu ahad’ is equivalent to one-third of the Qur'an.”

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: the matter or undertaking being considered
key_terms.ثُلُثَ الْقُرْآنِ: one-third of the Qur'an, indicating the merit of Surah al-Ikhlas
key_terms.دِينِي: my religion, meaning one’s religious well-being
key_terms.فَاصْرِفْهُ: turn it away and avert it
key_terms.فَيَسِّرْهُ: make it easy and facilitate it
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Surah al-Ikhlas, cited here for its recitation and virtue

ai.seo_question: What should a person recite and say when seeking Allah’s guidance before undertaking a matter?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a two-rak'ah prayer and du'a for one who intends to undertake a matter, asking Allah to facilitate it if it is good in religion and worldly life and to turn it away if it is not. It also states that any recitation may be used in the prayer, while recommending Surah al-Ikhlas and Surah al-Kafirun, and mentioning the great virtue of Surah al-Ikhlas.
